questions.q: Why does Mara present to Owen and Renee together instead of in two separate meetings?
options: To save time only
Because the firewall incident touches both of their concerns at once, and splitting the story would let each hear only half of it
Because Renee asked not to meet with Owen
Because Owen does not need to know about the incident
questions.explain: The incident is both an operational detail and a control failure, so a joint presentation keeps the full picture intact for both of them.

questions.q: What is the four-part structure of the presentation?
options: Apology, excuse, promise, closing
What was delivered, the real incident, the root cause, the fix and new control
Budget, timeline, staffing, next steps
Detection, triage, containment, eradication
questions.explain: The presentation follows delivered scope, then the incident, root cause, and fix plus control, in that order.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say presenting the incident candidly demonstrates the buildout worked?
options: Because the incident proves the SOC has no value
Because the SOC the team just built is exactly what caught the incident in the first place
Because Owen insisted on full disclosure regardless of outcome
Because Renee requires every incident to be reported regardless of relevance
questions.explain: The correlation rule and detection pipeline catching this incident is proof the buildout is functioning as intended.

questions.q: How does Mara adjust framing for Owen versus Renee?
options: She tells Owen a different root cause than she tells Renee
She changes no facts, but emphasizes the technical/operational shape for Owen and the control/evidence story for Renee
She only tells Renee about the incident, not Owen
She presents no technical detail to either of them
questions.explain: Both hear the same facts; emphasis shifts by role without changing any fact.

questions.q: What does the lesson explicitly warn against when presenting the incident?
options: Using the actual CIDR values and timeline
Vague language like 'a config issue was found and resolved,' over-apologizing, or blaming someone else
Mentioning the new standing control at all
Presenting to both stakeholders in the same meeting
questions.explain: Specificity builds credibility; vague language, blame-shifting, and over-apologizing undercut it.
